item.title: Stafford Supervisors Advance Land Conservation Efforts with PDR Program Update and New Tank Creek Easement
item.description: The Stafford County Board of Supervisors on March 17 received an update on its long-running Purchase of Development Rights program and unanimously approved a resolution accepting a co-holder open space easement on a forested preserve in the Widewater area, actions aimed at protecting rural lands and waterways.

item.title: Planning Commission Denies Bristow Substation, Removes Road Widening and Extension Plans Citing Noise, Health, Farmland, and Historic Concerns
item.description: In a marathon March 11, 2026, session that stretched past midnight, the Prince William County Planning Commission sided with western county residents on two high-stakes land-use matters, denying a major power substation tied to data-center growth and stripping three long-planned road projects from the Comprehensive Plan’s Mobility Chapter.

item.title: First Republican in Decades: Jeannie LaCroix Takes Woodbridge District Seat After Rescheduled Swearing-In
item.description: Jeannie LaCroix gave remarks at the March 17, 2026, meeting of the Prince William Board of County Supervisors. She took the oath for the Woodbridge District seat.

item.title: Stafford Board Approves $25M Literary Loan for Drew Middle School Replacement
item.description: The Stafford County Board of Supervisors unanimously approved the issuance of a $25 million literary loan at 3 percent interest to fund the replacement of Drew Middle School.

item.title: VRE Brings Back 4th of July Fireworks Trains After 10-Year Hiatus
item.description: Virginia Railway Express is reviving its Fourth of July fireworks trains after approximately 10 years to help celebrate America’s 250th birthday.

item.title: Animal Advocates Push for Three New Positions at Prince William Shelter in FY27 Budget - Potomac Local News
item.description: At the Prince William County Board of County Supervisors meeting on March 17, 2026, animal welfare advocates urged the board to add three full-time equivalent (FTE) positions to the county’s Animal Services Center in the proposed FY27 budget, at an estimated cost of approximately $225,000.

item.title: Fourth High-Speed Fatality in Two Years Prompts Rural Safety Warning from Prince William Supervisors
item.description: A recent crash in Nokesville has claimed another life on Prince William County’s rural roads, marking the fourth high-speed fatality in the Brentsville District in just two years.

item.title: Buc-ee’s Could Bring 2,174 Sunday Peak Vehicles to Exit 140 – Here’s How the Roads Would Change - Potomac Local News
item.description: If the proposed Buc-ee’s travel center at I-95 Exit 140 is approved, drivers in the Garrisonville area should prepare for significantly higher traffic volumes at key intersections they use every day, particularly during evening rush hour and on weekends, according to the newly released February 2026 (Version 6) Traffic Impact Analysis.
